question: A 12-year-old female with no past medical history is found to have an abnormal cardiovascular exam during routine physical examination at her pediatrician’s office. All other components of her physical exam are normal. During evaluation for potential causes for her abnormal exam, an echocardiogram with doppler is done that shows flow between the atria. Which of the following would would have most likely been auscultated as a result of the pathology on her echocardiogram?

options.opa: Increased splitting of S1 with inspiration
options.opb: Decreased splitting of S1 with inspiration
options.opd: Increased splitting of S2 with inspiration
options.ope: Splitting of S2 in inspiration and expiration

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Abnormal cardiovascular exam" -> "Echocardiogram shows flow between atria" -> "Indicates possible atrial septal defect (ASD)" -> "ASD leads to left-to-right shunt" -> "Increased blood flow to right atrium and right ventricle" -> "Increased right heart volume" -> "Increased splitting of S2 with inspiration" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Abnormal cardiovascular exam" -> "Echocardiogram shows flow between atria" -> "Suggests presence of a shunt" -> "Shunt causes altered hemodynamics" -> "Increased right heart volume" -> "Increased splitting of S2 with inspiration" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Abnormal cardiovascular exam" -> "Echocardiogram shows flow between atria" -> "Indicates potential atrial septal defect" -> "Increased pulmonary blood flow" -> "Increased right ventricular stroke volume" -> "Increased splitting of S2 with inspiration" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Abnormal cardiovascular exam" -> "Echocardiogram shows flow between atria" -> "Suggests atrial septal defect" -> "Increased right heart pressures" -> "Increased splitting of S2 with inspiration" -> 75%
analysis: The echocardiogram indicates flow between the atria, which suggests the presence of an atrial septal defect (ASD). In ASD, there is increased blood flow from the left atrium to the right atrium, leading to increased right heart volume and potentially affecting the timing of heart sounds. This condition typically results in increased splitting of S2 during inspiration due to the increased right ventricular stroke volume and prolonged right ventricular ejection time. Therefore, the most likely auscultation finding would be increased splitting of S2 with inspiration, making option opd the best choice.
